position: Organizational Issues and Budget: Personnel Challenges
proposal: The Mandate recommends that a conservative Administration rein in SBA efforts to expand the number of licensed Small Business Lending Companies, to create a new Mission-Based SBLC, and to drop the loan authorization requirement in the 7(a) and 504 programs in favor of reliance on lender documents. It asks that existing programs be brought under control and properly staffed, with outsourcing where private expertise is more efficient.

status_summary: On 2025-05-19 SBA announced a moratorium, effective immediately, on expansion of the Community Advantage program, reinstated the moratorium on new Community Advantage lending licenses, and said a new SOP would require existing lenders to meet financial stability standards and substantially increase capital reserves. SOP 50 10 8, announced 2025-04-22 and effective 2025-06-01, restored pre-2023 7(a) underwriting, collateral and equity injection requirements according to CRS, which does not describe any change to the loan authorization requirement; no rule restoring that requirement was found. SBA's Inspector General reported on 2026-09-17 (Report 26-14) that SBLCs had higher 7(a) default rates than other lenders, that SBA had 16 SBLC licenses as of 2025-04-05 after lifting the moratorium on new SBLC licenses in 2023, and that SBA had not conducted safety and soundness exams of SBLCs since 2023-04-04; SBA agreed to two recommendations and partially agreed to a third, with target dates in 2027.

timeline.event: SBA announced a moratorium on expansion of the Community Advantage program, reinstated the moratorium on new Community Advantage lending licenses, and said a new SOP would require higher capital reserves for existing lenders.
SOP 50 10 8 took effect for the 7(a) and 504 programs, restoring pre-2023 underwriting, collateral and equity injection requirements.

SBA Inspector General Report 26-14 found higher SBLC 7(a) default rates and no SBLC safety and soundness exams since 2023; SBA agreed to two recommendations and partially agreed to one, with target dates in 2027.

title: Rein in SBLC licensing growth, Mission-Based SBLCs and the end of loan authorizations
uncertainties: The SBA release of 2025-05-19 (No. 25-51) was re-read in this review on legacy.sba.gov: it imposes a moratorium on expansion of the Community Advantage program, reinstates the moratorium on new Community Advantage lending licenses and requires higher capital reserves under an unnumbered new SOP, and says nothing on loan authorization. The 2023 final rule (88 FR 21890) was read in full by the researcher and states that the Community Advantage SBLC type replaces the Mission-Based SBLC named in the proposal and removed the regulatory loan authorization definition; this review did not reopen it. The Inspector General report 26-14 was read in full by the researcher. The SOP 50 10 8 page on sba.gov could not be opened, so the link between the capital reserve standards and SOP 50 10 8 rests on the CRS Insight. A Federal Register API query for SBA documents containing loan authorization since 2025-01-20, run in this review, returned no documents, and a Small Business Lending Company query in an earlier pass returned none, so the finding that loan authorization was not restored is an absence of evidence.
